one_month_reasoning: Inside the window: Q3 2026 results on Oct 29 (before the open, call at 10:00 ET). Consensus is ~$9.9 EPS on ~$22.3B (MarketBeat), below Q2's $23.0B, so a sequential dip is already expected. The non-recurring Q2 rebate-estimate benefit (3% of US revenue, 10-Q) and European seasonality weigh on Q3. Against that, Q2 beat by ~$2 ($8.38 vs ~$6.07-6.55) even after $3.03 of IPR&D, Medicare Bridge starts reached 700k with 70% on Lilly (Ricks, Sep 21), and Foundayo is at ~47.5k weekly scripts and one-third of new oral starts. So the bar looks beatable, but the 2027 commentary will drive the reaction. Corrections from round 1: September was flat ($1,156.73 Aug 31 to $1,157.08 Sep 30, Twelve Data). The ~10% drop ran from the Aug 19 high to the Sep 11 low ($1,115.70) and has largely recovered, so there is no sell-off to rebound from and no reversal edge. The CagriSema decision (filed Dec 18, 2025, no PDUFA disclosed) most likely lands around mid-December, and the Foundayo T2D action (submitted Q2 2026) points to 2027, so neither is a window event. The 7th Circuit retatrutide opinion could come at any time, but it moves the long-term multiple, and I see it as two-sided. EDGAR shows no new 8-K since Aug 5. Net: nearly symmetric, with a slight up-tilt for a likely beat. Median ~$1,155 and monthly sigma ~11% (vs 35%/3.5 = 10%), widened for the earnings gap.

fair_value.method: 60% forward P/E (Oct-2027 NTM EPS ~$51.25 = 0.25 x 2027 $47.51 + 0.75 x 2028 $52.5, x 23.5x = ~$1204) plus 40% DCF valued at end-2027 (consensus revenue path, 34-35% FCF margin, 8% WACC, 3% terminal growth = ~$1,018). Blended to ~$1130 per share 12 months out.

I start at $52 and add $0.5 for the drift the supervisor and I both expect: 2027 revisions run 19 up / 4 down, the Q2 print of $8.38 beat a $6.07-6.55 consensus by ~$2 even after $3.03 of IPR&D, and Guggenheim lifted Foundayo to $1.8B/2027 and $3.7B/2028. I stay below the supervisor's $53: consensus 2028 revenue growth is only +11.6% and IRA prices hit Trulicity and Verzenio from 2028 (10-Q).

Today ~25.6x NTM (1149.85 / ~$44.9). By Oct 2027 consensus growth halves to ~10-12% (2028 revenue +11.6%), and the Medicare Bridge (700k starts, 70% on Lilly) ends Dec 31, 2027 with BALANCE Part D delayed indefinitely and no successor, so a 2028 Medicare coverage question will sit on the multiple at the horizon. In round 1 I leaned on management expecting coverage to continue; with no CMS successor on record I take 0.5 turn more off (24x to 23.5x). I do not go to 22.5x: revisions skew up, the tirzepatide compound patent runs to 2036 and retatrutide (BLA Q1 2027) is still ahead.
$7.0B is left on the $15B buyback; H1 2026 repurchases were 4.4M shares for $4.0B. That pace retires ~6-8M shares a year, net of grants.

methods.name: DCF
methods.inputs: 2027 revenue $101B (consensus); growth 11.6% (2028, consensus), then 9/7/6/5/4/4/3/3%; FCF margin 34% in 2028 and 35% after; WACC 8%; terminal growth 3%; net debt ~$15B at end-2027; ~880M shares. PV of 2028-36 FCF $306B plus PV of terminal value $606B = EV ~$911B. Retatrutide BLA/NDA ruling treated as a +/-$35-45 two-way branch that nets to zero.

inputs_detail.derivation: These replace my round-1 assumption of 20% growth in 2027. Consensus already reflects underlying US price of -9% (Q2) and the China NRDL price cuts.

Consensus FCF is $30.8B in 2027 (30%) and $38.6B in 2028 (34%). H1-2026 OCF of $16.0B less $5.3B capex shows the peak-capex trough (~25%); the 49-50.5% performance margin guide supports mid-30s once capex normalizes.

June 2026: total debt $54.9B (incl. $5.3B CP) less $9.0B cash and ~$3.9B investments. Consensus has net debt near zero by end-2027 ($0.8B). I hold $15B for continued buybacks and BD (Orna, Ajax, AtaiBeckley and a Scribe stake were all done in 2026).

Lilly's May 2026 notes priced at 4.375%-5.70% fixed coupons (pre-tax cost of debt ~5%). Beta of 0.45 implies a low CAPM cost of equity; I add a premium for policy risk (IRA selection, voluntary pricing agreement, MFN-style international alignment in the 10-Q) to reach 8%. 3% terminal growth because the franchise cycles to patent expiry (tirzepatide 2036+).

inputs_detail.value: BLA (12-yr) vs NDA (5-yr): roughly +/-$35-45 per share around the DCF; netted to zero at ~50/50
inputs_detail.derivation: The 7th Circuit (Lilly v. Kennedy, No. 26-1301) heard argument Sep 24, 2026 and has the case under advisement. A biologic classification extends retatrutide exclusivity to 12 years, adding to post-2032 FCF; an NDA path cuts it to 5. Retatrutide is a minority of 2032-36 FCF in my path, so each branch moves the DCF by roughly 3.5-4.5%. With no signal on the panel's leaning, I treat it as a coin flip, so the $1,018 point value is unchanged, but the ruling is an explicit scenario branch (see bull and bear).

bear.story: Price war deepens after the Jan 2027 resets (Novo Wegovy list $675, CVS co-preferred), so US underlying net price falls well beyond Q2's -9%. Novo's Wegovy pill (~170k weekly scripts, about 3.5-4x Foundayo) holds the oral market and CagriSema is approved in December. The 7th Circuit affirms the NDA path for retatrutide (5-year exclusivity), and the TRIUMPH-2 dysesthesia signal (4.5-7.3%) draws FDA questions. By mid-2027 no CMS successor to the Bridge is in sight, so investors price a 2028 Medicare cliff. 2027 EPS lands near $42 and 2028 near $45, at ~18x.

base.story: 2026 lands at or above the $85-87B guide. 2027 revenue is ~$101B and EPS ~$47-48 as volume (700k Bridge starts with 70% on Lilly, CVS Zepbound restoration, Foundayo at one-third of new oral starts, China and OUS) outruns price. Retatrutide BLA filed Q1 2027, with a decision in early 2028 on a standard review. The 7th Circuit outcome is mixed or still pending. The multiple compresses to ~23-23.5x on ~$51 NTM EPS as the 2028 Medicare question and slower growth weigh.

bull.story: The 7th Circuit orders or permits biologic classification (12-year exclusivity) and retatrutide gets an expedited review. Foundayo keeps gaining (Guggenheim's $1.8B 2027 path or better; T2D approval, ACHIEVE-4 CV safety). CMS signals coverage after the Bridge, and 2027 employer coverage improves. Beats keep coming at the Q2 pace (~$2 versus consensus), lifting 2028 EPS to ~$56 at ~27x.

thesis_break_reason: About 29% below spot and ~28% below my fair value: ~17.3x 2027 consensus of $47.51 and ~18x a reduced ~$45 NTM EPS, below the lowest Street target ($930). LLY has had drawdowns of 23-34% without broken fundamentals, so the price alone is not the signal. A break needs this level together with 2027/2028 EPS estimates being cut toward ~$42/$45. Likely causes: a structural US net-price reset well beyond -9% after the Jan 2027 resets; clear share loss to oral or next-generation rivals; the 7th Circuit affirming the NDA path for retatrutide, combined with a safety issue; or a confirmed 2028 Medicare coverage cliff with no successor to the Bridge. I keep $820 rather than the supervisor's $840: the gap is inside ordinary noise, and $820 sits nearer the depth of LLY's past non-fundamental drawdowns from a ~$1,200 base.

reasoning: Round 2, following the supervisor's review. (1) Facts corrected. September was flat, not -8% (Twelve Data closes: $1,156.73 Aug 31, $1,157.08 Sep 30); the drop ran from the Aug 19 high to the Sep 11 low and has largely recovered. Medicare Bridge uptake is 700k with 70% on Lilly (Ricks, CNBC Sep 21), not ~600k. The Q2 beat is real ($8.38 vs ~$6.07-6.55, despite $3.03 of IPR&D). The retatrutide classification appeal is a dated binary (7th Cir. No. 26-1301, argued Sep 24, under advisement). CagriSema most likely lands in December and Foundayo T2D in 2027, so neither falls in the October window. (2) Valuation. The supervisor called my consensus-anchored NTM EPS the best-supported input and I keep that approach, nudging 2028 from $52 to $52.5 for the upward revision skew and the verified ~$2 Q2 beat. NTM is ~$51.25. I take the forward multiple from 24x to 23.5x: with no CMS successor to the Bridge, a 2028 Medicare coverage question will weigh on the multiple at the horizon, where in round 1 I leaned on management's expectation of continuation. P/E = $1204. DCF is unchanged at $1,018; I treat the 7th Circuit ruling as a +/-$35-45 terminal branch that nets to zero. Blend: $1130 (was $1,140), about 1.5% below spot and ~2% below the supervisor's $1,160, since I keep 2028 EPS nearer published consensus and apply the Medicare-cliff discount. (3) Scenarios: $800 / $1,190 / $1,550 at 20 / 55 / 25%, mean ~$1,198; bull and bear are now built around the 7th Circuit outcome and the Medicare successor. (4) Ladder: lognormal with median ~$1,165 (fair value plus the positive skew of the scenarios and revisions), sigma 0.32 up / 0.34 down to fatten the policy and price left tail, and the deep tail held a little fatter than lognormal. P(>=1150) is 0.522 (was 0.53). (5) 1-month: the September-selloff narrative is dropped. Q3 on Oct 29 is the only scheduled catalyst; the bar looks beatable, and I tilt only slightly up. Median ~$1,155, sigma ~11%. Research limits: the CNBC pages returned 403, so the Ricks figures come from syndicated recaps (Yahoo, CNBC Foundayo piece). No option prices, implied volatility or anything under priors/ or round1_capped/ were used.
